extra.message: run_cmd() passes its argument directly to os.popen(), executing it as a shell command. Multiple GraphQL resolvers pass user-controlled input into this function (system_diagnostics cmd, system_debug arg, ImportPaste url), allowing arbitrary OS command injection / remote code execution.

resolve_system_diagnostics passes the user-supplied 'cmd' GraphQL argument to helpers.run_cmd() which executes it via os.popen(). In easy mode allowed_cmds() returns True for any command, enabling arbitrary OS command execution.

resolve_system_debug interpolates the user-supplied 'arg' GraphQL argument into a 'ps {}' command string passed to helpers.run_cmd()/os.popen(). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. '; rm -rf /') to execute arbitrary commands.

ImportPaste builds a 'curl --insecure {url}' shell command from user-controlled host/port/path/scheme arguments and runs it via helpers.run_cmd()/os.popen(). In easy mode strip_dangerous_characters() does nothing, allowing shell metacharacter injection and arbitrary command execution.

ImportPaste fetches an arbitrary user-controlled URL (built from host/port/path/scheme arguments) via curl with no validation of the destination. An attacker can target internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), or localhost, resulting in Server-Side Request Forgery.

resolve_pastes builds a raw SQL WHERE clause by string-formatting the user-controlled 'filter' GraphQL argument directly into a SQLAlchemy text() expression. This allows SQL injection (e.g. filter="' OR '1'='1") to read arbitrary data.

save_file() concatenates a user-controlled 'filename' (from the UploadPaste mutation) directly onto WEB_UPLOADDIR with no sanitization. A filename like '../../app.py' allows writing files outside the upload directory (path traversal / arbitrary file write).

get_identity() decodes the JWT with verify_signature=False and verify_exp=False, then trusts the 'identity' claim. The 'me' query and UserObject.resolve_password use this identity for authorization (returning the real password when identity=='admin'), so an attacker can forge any unsigned token to impersonate admin and bypass authentication/authorization.

resolve_delete_all_pastes deletes all paste records with no authentication or authorization check. Any anonymous client can invoke the deleteAllPastes query to destroy all data. Similar missing authorization applies to deletePaste, editPaste, and other mutations.

EditPaste mutation updates any paste by its 'id' argument without verifying the requester owns the paste or is authenticated. This allows Insecure Direct Object Reference, letting any user modify arbitrary pastes. DeletePaste (line 164) has the same flaw.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The JWT signing secret is hardcoded as 'dvga' (and Flask SECRET_KEY also 'dvga' on line 14). A weak, publicly-known secret allows attackers to forge valid JWT access/refresh tokens and Flask session cookies.
The Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded to the well-known value 'dvga', allowing attackers to forge or tamper with signed session cookies.

Default user accounts are seeded with hardcoded credentials: 'operator'/'password123' (line 64) and 'admin' with a weak password 'changeme' (random_password, lines 48-50). These predictable credentials allow trivial authentication bypass.
WEB_DEBUG defaults to True, enabling debug behavior in production. Combined with verbose error output this exposes internal state and can enable the Werkzeug debugger console.

format_custom_error attaches full Python stack traces (traceback.format_stack / format_exc) and source file paths into the GraphQL error 'extensions' returned to clients. This leaks internal implementation details, file paths, and execution state to attackers.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The Login mutation authenticates by directly comparing the supplied plaintext password against the stored password (User.query.filter_by(username=username, password=password)). Passwords are stored in plaintext (see setup.py seeding and User model), and admin's password is exposed via resolve_password, constituting sensitive data exposure / cleartext storage of credentials.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: sys.setrecursionlimit(100000) drastically raises the recursion limit; combined with GraphQL nested/recursive queries (depth protection disabled in easy mode) this enables resource-exhaustion denial-of-service.
